correctness.rationale: Every paired rim edge freezes to a monochrome pair after one update; \(a,b,m\) are exhaustive. The center switches in round one iff \(b>a\) and finishes opposite its initial vote iff \(b>n/2\) or \(b=n/2\) with \(m>0\); the resulting state is fixed and the two-step event is exactly \(a<b<n/2\). The central coefficient of \((2+z+z^{-1})^n\) gives the initial flip probability; a \(\operatorname{Bin}(n,1/4)\) tail minus the sole even-size tie exception gives the permanent flip probability, and the same argument works at bias p using \(\operatorname{Bin}(n,p^2)\). Stirling, bounded geometric tail ratios, and triangular-array CLTs justify all displayed asymptotics. Independent adjacency-list enumeration checked 174760 labelled states and 42 exact rational bias instances in the packaged verifier; these tests do not substitute for the all-size proof.

value.rationale: The natural center-plus-triangle-pairs network exhibits a robust difference between transient aggregate majority and stable aggregate majority: one half of unbiased starts reverse the global majority, despite a vanishingly small permanent center flip probability. At fixed biased peripheral input the two separate natural thresholds \(1/2\) and \(1/\sqrt2\) delimit a high-probability two-round reversal interval, with explicit Gaussian scaling. The exact fixed-state census and phase boundary describe nontrivial global attraction statistics on an infinite family, beyond a finite example or a generic period-two theorem.
